problems.title: Careful signs inside a cube
problems.question: Evaluate−[−(−2)³+(−1)³·8−(−1)⁸]³.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Odd powers keep a negative sign;even powers remove it.
steps: The bracket is 8−8−1=−1.
The expression is−(−1)³.

problems.title: A slower object on a longer trip
problems.question: The first object is 3 times as fast as the second and travels distance d in 3 minutes. How long does the second take for 3d?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Time is proportional to distance and inversely proportional to speed.
steps: A trip 3 times as far at one third the speed takes 9 times as long.
Time=3·9.

problems.title: Add a fourth number to a zero mean
problems.question: Three numbers have mean 0. Add the number 4. Find the mean of all four.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: The new total is 4, divided among 4 values.

problems.title: Product of two absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find the product of roots of|−x|+|x|=3.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: Roots are±3/2.
Their product is−9/4.

problems.title: Possible numbers of linear roots
problems.question: How many solutions can ax=2a+1 have?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: If a=0, the equation 0=1 has no solution.
Otherwise x=(2a+1)/a is the unique root.

problems.title: A right triangle’s altitude and bisector
problems.question: The angle between the altitude and angle bisector from a right-angle vertex is 22.5°. Find the acute triangle angles.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The bisector makes 45° with either leg;the altitude makes an angle equal to one acute triangle angle.
steps: Thus one acute angle differs from 45° by 22.5°.
The two complementary values are 22.5° and 67.5°.

problems.title: Divide integer powers
problems.question: Evaluate 12⁶·15⁴/(18⁷·10⁵).
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: Numerator=2¹²3¹⁰5⁴;denominator=2¹²3¹⁴5⁵.
Cancel to obtain 1/(3⁴·5).

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector and two perimeters
problems.question: The perpendicular bisector of AB meets BC at D. Perimeters ADC and ABC are 48 and 60. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: DA=DB because D is on the perpendicular bisector.
steps: Perimeter ADC=AD+DC+AC=DB+DC+AC=BC+AC.
Thus the difference between the two given perimeters is exactly AB.

problems.title: Which altitude statement is false?
problems.question: Select the false statement from the printed claims about altitudes, bisectors and medians.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: In an obtuse triangle, two altitude feet lie outside the triangle.
steps: Therefore the claim that all three altitudes are always inside is false.
Internal angle bisectors and medians lie inside. Adjacent supplementary-angle bisectors are perpendicular because their half-angles sum to 90°.
problems.answer: The claim that every altitude is always inside is false.
problems.note: The first claim says altitudes may fail to intersect:it is true for finite altitude segments in an obtuse triangle, but false for the complete altitude lines, which are concurrent. The same-side-interior-bisector claim also needs parallel underlying lines. These conventions are not fully stated.

problems.title: Distinct prime divisors of a product
problems.question: How many distinct prime divisors has 2002·2020?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: The distinct primes are 2, 5, 7, 11, 13, 101.

problems.title: Signs in an increasing list
problems.question: a<b<c<d<e and ac<0, bc<0. How many numbers are negative?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: If c<0, then a, b<c are also negative, and ac would be positive, a contradiction.
steps: Thus c>0. The two negative products force a<0, b<0.
The larger d, e are positive.

problems.title: Crossing equal segments and an angle
problems.question: AB and CD meet at O, AO=OD, CO=OB, CD=CB. The acute angle between AC and BD is 40°. Find ACB.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: SAS gives AC=BD, while AB=AO+OB=OD+OC=CD=CB. The configuration forms an isosceles trapezoid with bases AD, BC.
steps: Let ACB=t. Triangle ABC has AB=BC, so BAC=t.
The trapezoid symmetry makes its two legs AC, BD equally inclined to the bases. Their acute intersection angle is 180°−2t in this configuration.
Set 180°−2t=40° to obtain t=70°.

problems.title: A third price reduction
problems.question: A price is reduced 10%, then 25%, then by a third percentage. The final price is 46% below the original. Find the last reduction.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: The first two factors multiply to 0.675. Thus 1−r=.54/.675=.8.

problems.title: Surface area and volume scale
problems.question: Surface area cubed is proportional to volume squared. How does area change when volume increases 8-fold?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.

problems.title: An unchanged average then a removed box
problems.question: Adding a box of 7 pencils to n boxes leaves their average unchanged. Removing a14-pencil box afterward makes the average 6. Find n.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: An unchanged average upon adding 7 means the original mean was 7.
steps: After addition, total=7(n+1). After removing 14, there are n boxes averaging 6.

problems.title: Least sum with a fixed distance and magnitude ratio
problems.question: One number has twice the absolute value of another, and their distance is 3. Find the least possible sum.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Write the magnitudes 2t, t with t≥0.
steps: If signs agree, the distance is t=3;the smallest sum is−2t−t=−9.
If signs differ, the distance is 3t=3, so t=1, and the sums are±1.
Compare these cases.

problems.title: A bisector equal to a side
problems.question: A is the mean of the other two triangle angles. Bisector AD equals AB. Find C.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: BAD=30°. Since AD=AB, triangle ABD has base angles B=ADB=(180°−30°)/2=75°.

problems.title: A telescoping sum
problems.question: Evaluate 1/(2·3)+1/(3·4)+⋯+1/(8·9).
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: All middle terms cancel, giving 1/2−1/9.

problems.title: A bisector between parallel lines
problems.question: AB∥CD;AE bisects BAC and meets CD at E. CE=7.2 cm. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: Parallel-line angles give angle AEC=BAE;bisecting gives BAE=EAC.
steps: Triangle ACE therefore has equal angles at A, E, and opposite sides CE=AC.

problems.title: An internal bisector equals a remaining base piece
problems.question: In ABC, C=40°, B=20°. E∈BC and BE=AB. The A-bisector AD has length 2. Find CE.
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: A=120°. Triangle ABE is isosceles, so BAE=AEB=80°.
steps: Then EAC=40°=ACE, so AE=CE.
EAD=80°−60°=20°. Since angle AEC=100°, angle AED=80°;in ABD, the angle ADB is 100°, so ADE=80°.
Triangle ADE has equal angles at D, E, so AD=AE. Hence CE=AE=AD.

problems.title: A union of two integer sets
problems.question: How many three-digit positive integers are multiples of 4 or end in 4?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
steps: Multiples of 4:floor(999/4)−floor(99/4)=225. Ending in 4:90.
Their intersection has last two digits 04, 24, 44, 64, 84, with 9 choices of hundreds digit:45.
Union count=225+90−45.

problems.title: An impossible sign equation
problems.question: How many real roots has x/|x|=8?
problems.idea: Use the stated rule and check the result against the question.
formulas: The expression is undefined at 0, and equals 1 or−1 elsewhere.
steps: Neither value equals 8.
